Title: OTP threshold evaluated on amount plus fee instead of amount only
StepsToReproduce: 1. Initiate an international transfer of AED 24,990 with a fee of AED 26.25. 2. Submit the request.
ExpectedResult: No OTP is required because the transfer amount is below AED 25,000.
ActualResult: The service demands OTP because it evaluates 25,016.25 against the threshold.
RootCause: The threshold comparison used grossAmount rather than transferAmount in TransferValidator.java line 214.
Workaround: Customer completes the OTP; the transfer still succeeds.

Title: Balance check not repeated inside the posting transaction
StepsToReproduce: 1. Send two concurrent transfers of AED 6,000 from an account holding AED 10,000. 2. Fire both within 50 ms.
ExpectedResult: Exactly one transfer succeeds; the second is rejected with TRF-4003.
ActualResult: Both transfers post, driving the account AED 2,000 negative without an overdraft facility.
RootCause: Validation read the balance outside the database transaction and no pessimistic lock was taken on the account row.
Workaround: Manual reversal by the operations team followed by a customer call.

Title: Duplicate transaction ID under high concurrency
StepsToReproduce: 1. Run the load script at 400 TPS for 10 minutes. 2. Group the resulting transaction IDs and count duplicates.
ExpectedResult: Every transaction ID is unique.
ActualResult: 17 duplicate IDs observed across 240,000 transactions.
RootCause: The random suffix used java.util.Random seeded from the timestamp, so parallel threads on the same millisecond collided.
Workaround: None. Duplicates had to be corrected manually in reconciliation.

Title: Frozen account check skipped when the transfer is resumed after OTP
StepsToReproduce: 1. Create a transfer of AED 30,000 so it enters AWAITING_OTP. 2. Freeze the source account. 3. Submit a valid OTP.
ExpectedResult: The transfer is rejected with TRF-4011 because rules are re-evaluated at posting time.
ActualResult: The transfer posts successfully; the freeze is ignored on the resume path.
RootCause: The OTP verification handler called the posting service directly and bypassed the validation chain.
Workaround: Compliance manually reverses the transfer.

Title: OTP remains valid after three failed attempts
StepsToReproduce: 1. Create a transfer above AED 25,000. 2. Submit an incorrect OTP three times. 3. Submit the correct OTP.
ExpectedResult: The transfer moves to ABANDONED and the correct OTP is refused.
ActualResult: The correct OTP is accepted on the fourth attempt and the transfer posts.
RootCause: The attempt counter incremented but the status transition to ABANDONED was never persisted.
Workaround: None.

Title: Idempotency key accepted with a different request body
StepsToReproduce: 1. POST a transfer of AED 1,000 with key K1. 2. POST a transfer of AED 9,000 with the same key K1.
ExpectedResult: The second request is rejected with TRF-4012.
ActualResult: The second request returns HTTP 200 with the first transfer's details, so the customer believes AED 9,000 was sent.
RootCause: The gateway hashes only the idempotency key and not the request payload.
Workaround: Clients are instructed to generate a fresh UUID per request.

Title: Daily limit counter resets at 00:00 UTC instead of 00:00 GST
StepsToReproduce: 1. Transfer AED 100,000 between 00:00 and 04:00 GST. 2. Attempt a further transfer at 04:30 GST the same day.
ExpectedResult: The counter resets at 00:00 GST, so the customer has a fresh allowance only after midnight GST.
ActualResult: The counter reset at 04:00 GST, letting customers move up to AED 200,000 in one calendar day.
RootCause: The limit aggregation query used UTC date truncation while the reporting layer used GST.
Workaround: Limits temporarily reduced to AED 60,000 while the fix was deployed.

Title: Sanction screening timeout fails open
StepsToReproduce: 1. Stub the screening service to sleep for 10 seconds. 2. Submit a domestic transfer of AED 40,000.
ExpectedResult: The transfer is held in PENDING_COMPLIANCE and never auto-approved.
ActualResult: The circuit breaker opened and the transfer posted without screening.
RootCause: The fallback method returned CLEAR instead of raising a held status.
Workaround: Screening circuit breaker disabled in lower environments.

Title: Lower-case currency code rejected
StepsToReproduce: 1. Submit a transfer with currency set to "aed".
ExpectedResult: The code is normalised to upper case and the transfer proceeds.
ActualResult: The request is rejected with TRF-4010.
RootCause: The enum lookup was case sensitive.
Workaround: Client applications upper-case the value before sending.

Title: Error message discloses that a beneficiary is suspended
StepsToReproduce: 1. Attempt a transfer to a beneficiary in SUSPENDED status. 2. Inspect the response body.
ExpectedResult: A generic message is returned that does not reveal the specific status.
ActualResult: The response reads "Beneficiary is suspended by compliance", which leaks internal state.
RootCause: The internal reason string was mapped straight into the customer message field.
Workaround: None.

Title: Beneficiary owned by another customer returns 403 instead of TRF-4004
StepsToReproduce: 1. Authenticate as customer A. 2. Submit a transfer referencing a beneficiary belonging to customer B.
ExpectedResult: The request is rejected with TRF-4004 so that beneficiary ownership is not enumerable.
ActualResult: The request returns HTTP 403 with a distinct body, allowing an attacker to enumerate valid beneficiary IDs.
RootCause: Ownership check throws AccessDeniedException before the business validation chain runs.
Workaround: Rate limiting reduces the practical impact.

Title: Cut-off time not applied on UAE public holidays
StepsToReproduce: 1. Set the system date to a configured Eid holiday. 2. Submit a domestic transfer at 10:00 GST.
ExpectedResult: The value date is set to the next business day.
ActualResult: The value date is set to the holiday itself and the clearing file is rejected by the scheme.
RootCause: The holiday calendar table was populated for 2025 only and no fallback was implemented.
Workaround: Operations reschedules rejected items the following morning.

Title: IBAN comparison fails when the source contains spaces
StepsToReproduce: 1. Submit a transfer where the source IBAN contains spaces and the destination is the same IBAN without spaces.
ExpectedResult: Both are normalised and the transfer is rejected with TRF-4009.
ActualResult: The transfer is accepted and posts to the same account, creating an offsetting pair of entries.
RootCause: String equality was applied to the raw input without normalisation.
Workaround: The mobile client strips spaces before sending.

Title: Audit record missing for rejected transfers
StepsToReproduce: 1. Trigger a rejection under BR-001. 2. Query the audit store for the traceId returned in the error response.
ExpectedResult: An audit record exists naming BR-001 as the rejecting rule.
ActualResult: No audit record is written; only successful transfers are captured.
RootCause: The audit interceptor is bound to the success path of the posting service only.
Workaround: Application logs are retained for 90 days and used as an interim source.

Title: Cooling period measured from createdAt rather than activatedAt
StepsToReproduce: 1. Create a beneficiary and leave it in PENDING for 40 minutes. 2. Activate it. 3. Immediately transfer AED 20,000.
ExpectedResult: The transfer is rejected with TRF-4013 because activation was less than 30 minutes ago.
ActualResult: The transfer is accepted because the 30 minutes are counted from creation.
RootCause: The cooling-period calculation reads the wrong timestamp column.
Workaround: Fraud monitoring flags large first transfers for manual review.

Title: Daily limit consumed by transfers that later fail with TRF-5001
StepsToReproduce: 1. Force a core banking timeout on a transfer of AED 30,000. 2. Check the remaining daily allowance.
ExpectedResult: The failed amount is released back to the daily allowance.
ActualResult: The allowance stays reduced until midnight, blocking legitimate transfers.
RootCause: The limit was reserved before posting and never released on the failure path.
Workaround: Branch staff can raise a temporary limit increase.

Title: International transfers below AED 20,000 skip sanction screening
StepsToReproduce: 1. Submit an international transfer of AED 500. 2. Inspect the screening service call log.
ExpectedResult: Screening is invoked for every international transfer regardless of amount.
ActualResult: No screening call is made because only the amount threshold is evaluated.
RootCause: The screening trigger checks amount only and ignores transferType.
Workaround: Daily batch screening of all international transfers runs at 23:00 GST.

Title: Amount with three decimals silently rounded instead of rejected
StepsToReproduce: 1. Submit a transfer with an amount of 100.126.
ExpectedResult: The request is rejected with TRF-4008.
ActualResult: The amount is rounded to 100.13 and the transfer proceeds.
RootCause: JSON deserialisation applies half-up rounding before validation runs.
Workaround: None.

Title: dailyLimitRemaining in the response is stale under load
StepsToReproduce: 1. Submit five transfers in rapid succession. 2. Compare dailyLimitRemaining across the responses.
ExpectedResult: Each response reflects the allowance after that transfer.
ActualResult: Responses two to five repeat the value from response one for up to 3 seconds.
RootCause: The utilisation figure is served from a cache with a 3-second time to live.
Workaround: The mobile app refreshes limits from /v1/limits/utilisation after each transfer.

Title: OTP resend restarts the attempt counter
StepsToReproduce: 1. Fail the OTP twice. 2. Request a resend. 3. Observe attemptsRemaining.
ExpectedResult: attemptsRemaining stays at 1 because a resend does not reset the attempt counter.
ActualResult: attemptsRemaining returns to 3, allowing unlimited guessing through repeated resends.
RootCause: The resend handler recreates the OTP entity instead of updating the existing one.
Workaround: Resends are capped at two per transfer, limiting attempts to nine.
